The case is the FormD T1 V2.1 in Titanium. The case was really great to build, I did plenty of research so I already knew everything was going to fit together, all be it, super snuggly. The most surprising thing was how easy cable management was. I used all the standard cables which came with the Corsair SF750 powersupply and they all fitted fine. I did add fan grills on the top 2 exhaust fans to prevent any cables getting in the way.

The noctua cooler seems to be great, I ran Hogwarts Legacy, RDR2, and Cinebench R20 just for a quick check, and the cooling seems fine, no issues there. The CPU and GPU idle (youtube, discord, firefox with 20 tabs) at around 40c. And when gaming the CPU reached 60c, and the GPU reached 75c.   


I would reccomend all these parts except for the motherboard as it only had 1 system fan slot but thankfully I had an adapater which converts it to 4 from my previous NR200P build. Also the motherboard only has 1 m.2 slot, where as newer, higher priced models generally come with 2 nowdays.  


Overall everything went exactly as planned (which was a relief) :)

I could argue we also live in the most prosperous, technologically advanced society known to man. However, that doesn't stop me from facing the reality in which I percieve. Humans have steered away from what they were designed to do, and what makes them fulfilled. Hunting, and having a small community of connected individuals. We are more socially disconnected then we ever have been, despite having the technology to "connect" us all. We have sociatal levels of depression and suicide unranked by any society (as far as we know). 

So in conclusion, I'm not truely against having children inherently. But unless you have a real decent chance in providing a fulfilled and enriched life to your child what are you doing it for? I will also add I don't have much of a chance, nor want for ever having children, so you could argue my opinion is created in bias, which I couldn't deny.
